entity.name: Prit Ahir
entity.description: Individual developer based in India, requesting maintenance funding for FormSathi and the other MIT-licensed prototypes listed here, all developed with substantial AI assistance. No claim of paying users, revenue, verified adoption or fully on-device AI is made for any of them.

projects.name: FormSathi
projects.description: A local-first form-filling prototype with a guided English interview, field checklist, answer sheet and encrypted device-local Answer Vault. The existing repository includes a working local/manual path and automated tests. Optional Firebase/Gemini services are proprietary dependencies; personal content does not fall back to cloud inference. Real Gemini Nano execution remains unverified. The request supports existing software maintenance, security, accessibility and reproducible self-hosting, not an unbuilt idea.

projects.name: FreshCheck
projects.description: Stale-answer detector for AI applications: re-verifies LLM answers against live web sources and flags claims that have gone out of date. Early prototype with a working hosted demo; built with Bifrost and Tavily as proprietary service dependencies.

projects.name: Signal Room
projects.description: Incident-triage copilot that runs two open-weight models to analyze pasted logs, alerts and stack traces, cross-checks their assessments and suggests next steps. Early prototype from the Mozilla Otari hackathon.

projects.name: SwitchCart
projects.description: Buyer-consent layer for PayPal authorizations: when an item is unavailable, an AI proposes substitutions that the buyer must explicitly approve before capture. Early prototype with a hosted demo; uses proprietary PayPal APIs.

projects.name: SchemeSathi
projects.description: Voice-first agent that helps people check eligibility for Indian government schemes and explains required documents in simple language. Early prototype; not an official government service.

projects.name: emma-mcp
projects.description: MCP server giving AI agents access to multi-cloud spot compute through the emma API, so agent workflows can provision cheaper compute. Early prototype; depends on the proprietary emma service.

projects.name: VitalsGuard RT
projects.description: Deterministic real-time patient-vitals alarm engine prototype for QNX 8.0: rule-based threshold and trend alarms with no AI in the safety path, aimed at predictable latency. Early prototype, not a medical device.

projects.name: Open Agent Trust Badge
projects.description: Web component that publishes and verifies signed trust records from an agent-manifest.json, so websites can show a verifiable badge for their AI agents. Early prototype with a hosted demo.

projects.name: HackHunt Crew
projects.description: Four-agent crew that evaluates hackathon projects against judging criteria and shares one memory store, built for ContextCon 2026 with a Meko backend. Early prototype.

projects.name: FrameSheet
projects.description: Client-side zone-activity computer-vision engine stitched into a spreadsheet UI: camera regions map to cells and update them locally in the browser. Early prototype from Kiroween 2026; runs fully client-side.

projects.name: ShowUp
projects.description: Cross-chain event commitment escrow on NEAR: attendees stake a deposit refunded on check-in, using NEAR Intents and a DAO contract. Early prototype with a hosted demo on testnet-grade infrastructure.

projects.name: Escalating Rebuttal Flip Curves
projects.description: Code, data and paper for a research sprint entry studying how repeated rebuttals flip AI model answers, with reproducible experiment scripts and result data.

channels.description: Grant payout method to be agreed privately after selection. No payment credentials are published in this manifest.

plans.name: 12-week maintenance and accessibility pilot
plans.description: 12-week FormSathi maintenance: triage dependency advisories, update packages, add privacy regression tests (wks 1-4); improve offline/manual path, keyboard/screen-reader access, vault recovery docs (wks 5-8); pilot with five consenting adults on fictional data, fix critical issues, tag a documented release (wks 9-12). Budget: maintainer 240h x INR 500 = INR 120000; security review INR 15000; testing/data INR 9000; hosting/backup INR 6000. Maintainer commits ~20 h/week plus one community update.

plans.name: 12-week maintenance of the additional prototypes
plans.description: 12-week maintenance across the other listed prototypes: dependency and security triage, tests, documentation, reproducible setup and tagged releases. Budget: maintainer 240h x INR 500 = INR 120000; independent security review INR 15000; testing/data INR 9000; hosting/backup INR 6000. Milestones: weeks 1-4 dependency and security triage with tagged releases; weeks 5-8 tests and documentation; weeks 9-12 reproducible setup, release hardening and a public maintenance report.
